title: Infinite Grief! Amazing Woe
description: Infinite Grief! Amazing Woe in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 95, headed “Look on him whom they pierced, and mourn”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In-fin-ite grief! a-ma-zing woe! Be-hold my bleed-ing Lord: Hell and the Jews con-spir'd his death, And us'd the Ro-man sword.

lines: Hell and the Jews conspir'd his death,
O the sharp pangs of smarting pain
When knotty whips and ragged thorns
But knotty whips and ragged thorns
In vain I blame the Roman bands,
'Twere you, my sins, my cruel sins,
Each of my crimes became a nail,
'Twere you that pull'd the vengeance down
Break, break, my heart, O burst mine eyes!
Strike, mighty grace, my flinty soul,
And deep repentance drown mine eyes

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
